summary: Built X_p = flag complex on the words of p with edges between words sharing a coordinate value, σ(t,u,v) = (t,v,u) (A ↦ A*). For p ≡ 1 (8), p ≤ 120, X_p is F_2-acyclic (all reduced Betti numbers 0), and σ has no fixed vertex (u = v is impossible for prime p). Smith's theorem is then satisfied only by σ-invariant edges {(t,u,v),(t,v,u)} (these always exist, as the two words share t), so the forced fixed point is a trivial midpoint and carries no certificate information (scripts/z52d_p2_NC3_topo.py).
not_done: Did not use the 'near-solution' complex or p > 120; complex choice (share-a-letter flag complex) is mine, the item left it open.
next: None; a useful Smith argument needs an involution with fixed points that are not forced by the t-coordinate.

summary: Flag complex of F_p has no triangles (0 over 211 primes ≡1 (4), p≤3000) and explicit free-face edge collapses (vertex of degree 1 with its edge) reduce each component to one vertex: 5933 collapses, 0 critical edges, critical vertices = b0 = 289892 and b1 = 0 (CERTIFIED computation). The Morse reduction is therefore perfect and carries no information beyond the forest structure.

summary: Goldbach for Gaussian/Hurwitz/Eisenstein primes: arXiv:1606.05958 (positive-coefficient sums) and arXiv:2309.14249 (sector versions, almost-all) — no pointwise statement for ES.

Round 3: discriminant D=-16c^2d, 1<=c,d<=20 (400 pairs), class number by reduced-form count; witness = divisor f of p^2+4c^2d with 1<f<N and f = -p mod 4cd, primes p=1 mod 4 up to 10^4 (609). Witness cases have even h in all 9371 observations, which looked significant (chi^2 p=8e-7), but h depends only on (c,d), so the 243600 per-prime observations are not independent. At the level of pairs there is exactly one odd-h pair, (c,d)=(1,1), h=1, with witness rate 0; Fisher p=1.0. No class-group parity correlation is supported; the earlier 'significant' value is a one-pair artifact.
not_done: Larger (c,d) ranges where odd class numbers occur more often; the witness predicate is taken from the item's Type-I form (f | p^2+4c^2d, f = -p mod 4cd) as I read it.
next: Test the same statistic over a larger (c,d) box (d squarefree, c up to 200) so that odd-h pairs are numerous enough for a pair-level test.

summary: Measured E_T(p)=Σ_{t≤T}[D_t⁻(tp+1)−τ(tp+1)/φ(t)] (D_t⁻ = #{d|tp+1: d≡−1 mod t}) over the 117 primes ≡1(4) in [10⁵,1.025·10⁵], T≤400 with divisors by spf factorisation. Its spread over p grows like T^0.37 (fit T=25…400), so no worse than independent level errors (T^0.5). The mean is a systematic bias (−14 at T=25 to −54 at T=400) that FRONTIER §2.3 ties to the odd-character part of D⁻−D⁺; I did not separate it numerically. No Kloosterman sum was evaluated and no Weil/Kuznetsov bound was checked.
not_done: Odd-character main term not subtracted; Kloosterman sums S(m,n;c) not written or bounded; one window only (p≈10⁵).
next: Subtract the §2.3 odd-character term from D⁻ and refit the T-exponent over p≈10⁶–10⁷.

Identity checked: 4/p = 1/((p−1)/4) − 1/(p(p−1)/4) holds, so signed relaxation is trivial. Exact enumeration of all nonzero-integer solutions of 4/13 = 1/x+1/y+1/z with max|·| ≤ B: 36, 78, 108, 120, 120 for B = 100, 300, 1000, 3000, 10⁴ (63 with exactly one negative entry at B=10⁴). The count saturates, so there is no growth to measure; the proposed 'move into the positive cone' step was not attempted.

summary: I applied the standard determinant-2 coset representatives to the ES word w=(2,2,3), with n=7 and γ=[[3,7],[2,5]]: γ·diag(2,1)=[[6,7],[4,5]], γ·diag(1,2)=[[3,14],[2,10]], and γ·[[1,1],[0,2]]=[[3,13],[2,12]]. All have determinant 2, whereas the ES word matrices in METAPLECTIC_ES §1 have determinant 1; none is itself a word matrix without an additional normalization/reduction not specified in the proposal.
evidence: inline T₂ coset multiplication on w=(2,2,3)

summary: Checked arXiv:1311.4600 ('Small gaps between primes', Maynard, 2013): bounded gaps between primes are proved by the sieve. The parity barrier and the sieve input do not give an ES count; the item has no ES-side step.

Hit structure of the word parametrisation: for fixed (t,u) the hit condition is (tu−1) | (p+u) (equivalent to a word tuv−u−v=p with integer v). Over tu≤200: hard primes 409, 577, 5569, 9601 have 26, 32, 20, 19 hits (t,u); controls 1009 and 10009 have 21 and 52 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_C.py, C_out.txt). The hits at t=1 are u∈{2,3,6,11,…}. No orbit-like propagation between primes was identified (hits depend only on p mod tu−1, so propagation across primes is the congruence structure itself).
not_done: Orbit analysis under p↦p+L for L=lcm(tu−1).
next: Test whether hit sets at p and p+L coincide (they do by construction) and whether hard-prime hit counts differ from controls at larger T.
